prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Memory from EARLIER parts of the document (do not extract facts from it; use it only to resolve names, aliases and who produces an item):
Offshore wind farm O&M concept. Boundary: turbines, array, Offshore Substation (alias Morrowick), export connection to Grid Interface Relay (external). Out of scope: public grid beyond connection; non-farm port ops. Offshore equipment, services and shore decisions are separated; interfaces have defined change-management responsibilities; supervisory functions are distinct from planning; personnel keep procedural, safety and engineering authority; defined handoffs keep dispatch, marine judgment, work supervision and stores control accountable. Turbine: Turbine Controller (alias Glassfin; produces Pitch Deviation Notice), Pitch System, Rotor Brake Unit, Converter Cabinet, Nacelle Condition Monitor, Turbine Sensor Bus; Blade Inspection Drone. Substation: Main Transformer, Export Cable Monitor. Shore: SCADA Gateway (alias Juniper Vale; supervisory communications within its control scope), Shore Control Room (alias Amber Quay; operational oversight, shore coordination point), Maintenance Planning Engine (alias Thistle Crown), Fleet Dispatch Console (alias Sable Orchard; vessel assignments/status). Vessels: Crew Transfer Vessel (alias Kestrel Bay), Daughter Craft, Service Operations Vessel; Helideck; Vessel AIS Receiver (produces Position Quality Flag when integrity checks fail or confidence is below threshold). Personnel Tracking Console; North/South Access Scanners; Warehouse System (alias Mosslight); Spares Hub; Work Permit Portal. Cybersecurity Gateway (alias Quiet Harbor): boundary between authorized shore services and offshore networks; only approved protocols, destinations and accounts; external connectivity denied by default. Admin access uses individual authenticated role-based accounts; privileged sessions are time-limited, logged and reviewed. Losing the boundary restricts remote admin without bypassing local protections. Security logs are protected; networks are segmented. Metocean Buoy (alias Copper Finch): measures wind, waves, current, air temperature and pressure; its logger timestamps and buffers data; time sync and sensor health are checked. Actors: HSE Officer (verifies safety controls), Field Supervisor (coordinates offshore tasks, informs Duty Planner), Duty Planner, Marine Coordinator, Vessel Master (navigation and transfer go/no-go), Weather Analyst (reviews forecast limits for access and work), Storekeeper, Port Agent, Cybersecurity Analyst (monitors gateway events), SCADA and Control Engineers. External: Weather Service (alias Pale Lantern; Squall Window Bulletin; uses validated observations), grid ops, ports, emergency services. Modes: commissioning, normal service, planned and unplanned maintenance, major…

Document units:
S121: Interfaces are tested after configuration changes to confirm that permitted functions remain available and prohibited paths remain blocked.
S122: Operational procedures identify the authority for approving access, responding to alarms, and returning affected services to normal operation.
S123: This section describes turbine control and remote observation during offshore operations.
S124: Vessel AIS Receiver is designated Blue Granite for this operational concept.
S125: Blade Inspection Drone is designated Larkspur for this operational concept.
S126: Duty Planner prepares the Transfer Manifest Addendum to capture approved vessel deployment changes.
S127: Glassfin adjusts turbine output within approved operating limits and blocks commands that conflict with active protection conditions.
S128: Pale Lantern issues forecast updates that support timing decisions for remote observation and field work.
S129: Turbine Controller executes authorized control actions and reports its operating state through established control interfaces.
S130: Pitch System changes blade angle in response to turbine control commands and local protection logic.
S131: Converter Cabinet manages electrical conversion while observing equipment limits and protective interlocks.
S132: Nacelle Condition Monitor provides equipment measurements for ongoing assessment of turbine health.
S133: SCADA Gateway presents turbine status and control availability to authorized shore personnel.
S134: Shore Control Room provides a staffed location for supervisory control and operational review.
S135: Control Engineer reviews alarms and operating conditions before issuing a remote command.
S136: Remote commands are subject to role-based authorization and are recorded for later operational review.
S137: Local protection functions retain priority when remote requests conflict with safe operating limits.
S138: Control availability is checked before remote operation begins and after relevant configuration changes.
S139: Vessel AIS Receiver collects vessel position broadcasts to support marine traffic awareness.
S140: The receiver maintains a time-stamped view of nearby vessel movements when broadcast coverage is available.
S141: Marine Coordinator uses the available traffic picture to support coordination of offshore movements.
S142: Blade Inspection Drone captures close-range visual observations of accessible blade surfaces.
S143: Blade Specialist plans inspection passes to provide consistent coverage of areas selected for examination.
S144: Captured imagery is reviewed for visible surface changes and potential maintenance concerns.
S145: Field Supervisor considers remote observations alongside site conditions before recommending follow-up work.
S146: Drone operation is suspended when weather, visibility, or equipment status makes flight unsafe.
S147: Remote observations supplement field assessment and do not replace required physical inspections.
S148: Maintenance Planning Engine can use reviewed condition information when prioritizing future maintenance activities.
